title: UPI MDR Row: Gold traders set to protest on Oct 15 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Kerala Gold and Silver Merchants Association (KGSMA) will stage a protest before Central Government offices on October 15, demanding the withdrawal of merchant discount rates (MDR) on UPI transactions.

K.Surendran, State president and S. Abdul Nazar, general secretary of the association said that the imposition of UPI charges a “double blow” to the gold trade sector, which is already grappling with rising business costs alongside soaring gold prices.

Traders do not see an increase in profits simply because gold prices are rising. Imposing UPI charges—on top of high capital investment, price volatility and market sluggishness—threatens the very survival of small- and medium-sized jewellery businesses. Even minor charges translate into significant financial burdens for high-value gold jewellery transactions, they said.

The government, which promotes “Digital India” and cashless transactions, should rectify its approach of imposing additional financial burdens on merchants who accept digital payments. While digital transactions help ensure transparency and tax compliance, it is unfair to impose the associated costs on merchants, the association said.

The association demanded that digital payments should be encouraged and merchants should not be burdened with the costs. A merchant’s profit should not be calculated based on the price of gold, they said.
